summary: Discovery focused on model selection for Meridian Health's patient-facing summarization and triage product. Key considerations: context length, multilingual support (EN/ES/pt/fr + some zh), tool/function-calling for EHR lookup, latency vs cost tradeoffs, and deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC). Agreed next steps include pricing, benchmarks, and a security follow-up.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-10 14:30 UTC — Duration 46 mins. Attendees: Austin (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Sam (CTO), Lina (Lead ML), Mark (Security), Jordan (PM)

[00:00] Austin: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh i'll kick off, this is a discovery to understand meridian's model needs, right? context lengths, multilingual, tool calling, and whether hosted / dedicated / private is the right fit. quick intros?
[00:12] Sam: yeah sam patel, cto, quick note — we're building a patient summarization + triage assistant, it needs to pull from EHR snippets, call a scheduling service, and respond in english/spanish/portuguese.
[00:25] Lina: lina here; i'm the lead ml eng, i'll own the evaluation. main concerns are latency under 400ms p95 for short flows, and handling long context for discharge summaries (up to 60k tokens).
[00:38] Mark: dr mark chen, security — SOC2 is a must, also we're evaluating KMS, audit trails, and VPC options for PHI.
[00:50] Priya: great, thanks. quick clarifying q — when you say 60k tokens, is that full sequence you need for a single call or you'd prefer streaming/segmented context?
[01:02] Lina: ideally single call for recall/referencing, we do a lot of patient history concatenation. But we'd consider a hybrid if cost/latency are prohibitive.
[01:14] Austin: cool. at a high level redwood offers hosted (fast to try), dedicated (reserved gpu capacity), and private (vpc/on-prem). for 60k contexts we typically look at models with extended context or use our kv/prefix caching + retrieval to keep cost down.
[01:28] Sam: what open models support that context today? we've been testing a few internally — Llama2 variants, Mistral, and some newer 32k-window forks.
[01:40] Priya: right now there's a mix — some forks offer 32k or 64k windows, e.g. LlamaX-32k, Mistral-Chat-32k, and we're seeing community builds with 64k. we also offer model fallbacks and kernel selection to prioritize latency. important distinction: longer context often increases memory pressure and latency — but we can split attention with retrieval.
[02:02] Jordan: tool-calling — we need function calls to trigger EHR lookups and appointment booking. is that supported on hosted models? any limitations?
[02:14] Austin: yes, function/tool calling is supported across hosted and dedicated. private requires some config but we support structured tool calls and deterministic JSON outputs. there are differences in model capabilities — some open models have better structured output by default.
[02:28] Sam: latency vs cost — if we go hosted and pick a 40B model with 32k context, what are we looking at for p95? ballpark.
[02:40] Priya: ballpark depends on batch size and tokens per request; for single-request small outputs with 32k context at dedicated GPU it's sub-300ms p95 on our optimized kernels for some models. hosted with multi-tenant can be slightly higher; that's why we suggest dedicated for predictable tail latency.
[02:56] Lina: can you quantify cost differences? we have monthly budgets and need to justify dedicated commit.
[03:04] Austin: we'll share a cost sheet; rough rule: hosted per-token is higher but no commit; dedicated reduces per-token cost once you hit throughput commitments. we'll send committed capacity pricing.
[03:15] Mark: security — our main blocker for hosted is PHI policy and auditability. does hosted support customer-managed KMS or do you encrypt with your keys?
[03:27] Priya: hosted supports bring-your-own-key via integration with major KMS on enterprise plans? we can also offer private deployment (VPC) where keys stay in customer's cloud. we have audit logs and per-route tracing in Console.
[03:41] Sam: ok good. another item: multilingual quality. Spanish and Portuguese are high priority, Chinese lower but present. any models better out-of-the-box?
[03:53] Priya: some models like Mistral-family and later LlamaX tend to have stronger multilingual performance; we can run targeted evals. we also surface model quality profiles in the catalog.
[04:07] Jordan: what about hallucinations when pulling EHR data and generating summaries — can you pin model versions and roll back quickly?
[04:16] Austin: yes — model pinning and rollout controls are part of the console; we support canary and automatic fallback to safer model variants. also quality monitoring with prompt-based evals so you can detect regressions.
[04:31] Lina: about the 60k context — you mentioned retrieval. what's the recommended pattern? chunk + retrieval or use a long-context model?
[04:41] Priya: recommended is retrieval-augmented generation: store embeddings, retrieve relevant chunks, use prefix KV cache for recent conversation. For discharge docs where full chronology matters, we can stitch summaries + retrieval to emulate long context and keep latency reasonable. we can also run a 64k model if you deem it necessary for certain flows.
[04:59] Sam: performance for tool calls — does function calling add extra latency? e.g., call EHR API then resume.
[05:08] Priya: the orchestration adds network hops; we minimize by local caching and batching calls. some customers do prefetching so the model can call quickly. redwood provide hooks for synchronous and asynchronous tool calls.
[05:23] Speaker 1: (inaudible) ...
[05:30] Mark: auditability — do we get per-request payloads in logs (redacted) and ability to forward logs to our SIEM?
[05:40] Austin: yes, enterprise plans support configurable logging retention and log forwarding, with PII redaction options.
[05:48] Lina: on benchmarks — Priya, can you run both LlamaX-32k and a Mistral-40B variant with our prompts? we want throughput metrics and p95 tail.
[06:00] Priya: absolutely; we'll need sample prompts and representative concurrency. also let us know expected output lengths.
[06:08] Jordan: ok we'll share 10 prompts of varying lengths and expected outputs.
[06:14] Sam: curious about quantization — can dedicated reduce memory so we can run larger models cheaper?
[06:23] Priya: yes, we support quantized variants and recommend quantization profiles per workload. dedicated + quantization often unlocks 2-3x cost reductions depending on precision. we'll propose profiles in the benchmark report.
[06:37] Austin: any regulatory constraints beyond PHI and SOC2? data residency?
[06:42] Mark: we need EU data residency for EU patients; most of our infra is US but we have EU cloud for data locality.
[06:50] Priya: Redwood Dedicated and Private can ensure regional routing; hosted also has region selection for enterprise tenants.
[06:58] Sam: what about model updates and drift — how are rollouts tested?
[07:04] Austin: we provide rollout controls and can tie regressions to prompt sets. customers set evaluation thresholds; automatic rollback is possible.
[07:12] Lina: for tool calling format — we need deterministic JSON for downstream parsers. some models return loose text; others can be strict. can Redwood enforce structured outputs?
[07:23] Priya: yes we have a structured output layer and post-validators. for models that are flaky we'll use function calling and schema validation with retry/fallback.
[07:35] Jordan: do you have pre-built connectors for FHIR/EHR systems or is that customer work?
[07:41] Austin: we have example connectors and reference implementations; a few platform partners for deeper integrations. we'll share a connector repo link.
[07:50] Speaker 2: (crosstalk)
[07:55] Sam: timeline — if we start a pilot, how long to test and what does success look like?
[08:02] Priya: pilot typically 4 weeks: week 1 provision + smoke tests, week 2 run benchmarks and iterate, week 3 integrate tool calls, week 4 scale and evaluate metrics. success criteria: p95 latency < 400ms for short flows, acceptable cost per call, <2% structured output failures, and security sign-off.
[08:20] Lina: that seems reasonable. what about tokenization differences across models — does Redwood normalize?
[08:27] Priya: we surface tokenization metrics and effective context (tokens per KB). we recommend models based on token efficiency for your doc types; we'll include tokenization comparisons in the benchmark.
[08:40] Sam: competitors — we've looked at OpenAI + Anthropic for safety and quality, but owning private infra is attractive for cost. what's the sweet spot?
[08:51] Austin: many customers start hosted for eval, then move to dedicated as throughput grows; private is chosen by those with strict PHI/regulatory needs. We'll show cost curves in the pricing workbook.
[09:03] Jordan: any red flags for us? like models that absolutely fail on medical phrasing?
[09:09] Priya: older models without clinical fine-tuning will hallucinate more. we'll test a medically-tuned retrieval pipeline and measure factuality. also recommend human-in-the-loop for high-risk outputs.
[09:23] Sam: okay let's recap — we need: pricing, a benchmark run of two models with our prompts, security docs (SOC2, KMS integration, audit log examples), and a follow up security meeting.
[09:36] Austin: yep i'll send the pricing + links to our docs (https://redwood.ai/docs/benchmarks, https://redwood.ai/security). Priya will take the benchmark action.
[09:46] Priya: i'll schedule the deep-dive, need credentials and sample prompts; will run with LlamaX-32k and Mistral-40B quantized.
[09:56] Mark: i'll put together questions about KMS and retention to share.
[10:02] Lina: minor thing — can we get a demo of the Console's rollout UI during deep-dive?
[10:09] Austin: sure, we'll demo rollouts, per-route dashboards, and tracing.
[10:14] Speaker 1: thanks all.

[10:18] End recap and next steps (as above).

Notes on transcription: occasional garble, some proper nouns mis-transcribed (LlamaX vs Llama2 forks), but content preserved. References: pricing workbook (link to be shared), benchmark playbook, connector repo.
